input.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

ref_file = r"C:\Users\sandeeppawar\Downloads\aida-eval\data\file_generation_en\reference\FG_140\external_Amazon_Jan-Jun_sales_data_simulation_res.xlsx"
pred_file = r"C:\Users\sandeeppawar\Downloads\aida-eval\runs\aida-ctrl\work\FG_140\external_Amazon_Jan-Jun_sales_data_simulation.xlsx"

ref_df = pd.read_excel(ref_file, sheet_name=0)
pred_df = pd.read_excel(pred_file, sheet_name=0)

# For a comprehensive check, let's compare column by column statistics
# This is more efficient than row-by-row comparison for 2598 rows

comparison_results = []

for col in ref_df.columns:
    ref_col = ref_df[col]
    pred_col = pred_df[col]
    
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(ref_col):
        # For numeric columns, compare statistics
        ref_sum = ref_col.sum()
        pred_sum = pred_col.sum()
        ref_mean = ref_col.mean()
        pred_mean = pred_col.mean()
        ref_std = ref_col.std()
        pred_std = pred_col.std()
        
        sum_match = np.isclose(ref_sum, pred_sum, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        mean_match = np.isclose(ref_mean, pred_mean, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        std_match = np.isclose(ref_std, pred_std, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        
        if sum_match and mean_match and std_match:
            comparison_results.append(f"{col}: ✓ Stats match")
        else:
            comparison_results.append(f"{col}: ✗ Stats differ (sum_match={sum_match}, mean_match={mean_match}, std_match={std_match})")
    else:
        # For text columns, compare value counts
        ref_counts = ref_col.value_counts().sort_index()
        pred_counts = pred_col.value_counts().sort_index()
        
        if ref_counts.equals(pred_counts):
            comparison_results.append(f"{col}: ✓ Value counts match")
        else:
